definitions.engagedParticipation: Worth 30%. Includes active listening as well as contributions to class discussion that demonstrate thoughtfulness, build on others' contributions, and draw on course readings and conversations. Students are asked to be fully present and engaged during class, in both discussions and in-class exercises. Students are also encouraged to post on the Canvas discussion forum to share resources, reflections, and ideas between classes. Multi-tasking during class is strictly prohibited — if you have other things to do, do them elsewhere; multi-tasking contributes negatively to collective learning and is reflected in participation scoring.
definitions.writtenAssignments: Four written assignments that build on each other as students progress along the ten-stage framework in the social entrepreneurship textbook. The essay on personal framing is a personal reflection requiring no outside research. The problem statement and logic model require research per the textbook guidelines. The final reflection synthesizes course learnings including previous assignments, readings, in-class exercises, and discussions. Further details, guidelines, and rubrics for each assignment are posted on Canvas. All assignments must be uploaded on Canvas at least one calendar date before class.
definitions.fourModules: The course develops the innovation mindset and skillset across four modules: Problem, People, Project, and Policy. It refers to the ten-stage framework in the textbook 'Social Entrepreneurship: Building Impact Step by Step' and other social innovation frameworks. There are no prerequisites.
definitions.aiPolicy: The purpose of the assignments is for students to apply their own critical thinking and synthesis skills; therefore, USE OF AI IS NOT PERMITTED IN THIS COURSE. Students must write papers independently from one another and cite sources consulted using Chicago Manual of Style guidelines. Students may refer to material from course sessions using parenthetical citations (example: 'Course Meeting, November 5, 2026'). Students must cite any ideas taken from another source, published or not. Failure to comply is considered a serious disciplinary matter.
definitions.textbooks: Chahine, T. Social Entrepreneurship: Building Impact Step by Step. Routledge (2023). Drummond, S. Holy Clarity: The Practice of Planning and Evaluation. Rowman & Littlefield (2009). All readings can be found in the Course Reserves tab in Canvas.
definitions.arrivalLogistics: If you are coming from another part of campus, arrive at Yale Divinity School around 1pm, or 1:15 at the latest, to get your bearings and get settled by the time class starts. One of the instructors will meet students at the YDS main entrance — between the Living Village and the exterior of Sterling Divinity Quad — to direct them to SG58 between 1-1:15 before the first two sessions.

gradingPolicy: Engaged Participation 30%; Essay on Personal Framing (due Sept 16, 500 word limit) 15%; Problem Statement (due Sept 30, 800 word limit) 15%; Logic Model (due Nov 18, tabular/visual template provided in textbook) 20%; Final reflection (due Dec 9, 1000 word limit) 20%.
